newsitem.title: USA: Nutrition Medical Q1 expenses rise.
newsitem.headline: Nutrition Medical Q1 expenses rise.

text.p: Nutrition Medical Inc said Tuesday its expenses rose in the first quarter due to costs associated with its growth plan.
New products from the company's purchase of Elan Pharma Inc helped first quarter results, the company said.

"The new products had a positive effect on quarterly sales, however, there was also an associated increase in fixed costs," William Rush, chief executive of the nutrition products compabny, said in a news release.
"In addition, investments in product development efforts and staffing needs relative to our aggressive growth plans increased expenses disproportionally to one year ago.

"We are encouraged, though, by the initial revenue growth derived from these investments and we anticipate further growth, particularly within the clinical division, as our products gain wider distribution."
The company also said it is on target with developing an infant fomula, which it expects to release in late 1997 or early 1998.
Earlier Tuesday, Nutrition Medical reported a net loss of $440,021, or $0.08 a share in the quarter, compared to a loss of $82,710, or $0.03 a share, a year ago.
